newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa trade surprised by Q3 grind rise.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa trade surprised by Q3 grind rise.

text.p: A seven percent rise in the German cocoa grind in the third quarter to 65,824 tonnes was more than traders had expected, they said on Wednesday.
"It's a very good result, I expected flat to slightly higher," one said after German Confectionery Association BDS released the figure.
"I'm hearing there is good capacity utilisation at many processing plants."
The grind was at 65,824 tonnes, 7.0 percent more than the 61,523 tonnes in the third quarter of 1995.
Traders said export business had been high, especially to eastern Europe, and the cool summer had encouraged chocolate consumption here.
One suggested price wars had depressed the retail price of finished products and consumers had responded by buying more chocolate.
But another trader said, "I doubt that. The price fights have been a feature of the market for years, I think this latest figure demonstrates a solid rise in consumption."
The Dutch grind last Friday was up 16.69 percent at 99,549 tonnes.
Traders said if the U.S. grind confirmed the positive figures in western Europe -- they believed Benelux countries, Italy and France also saw higher consumption -- the cocoa market could turn higher.
"I don't think there will be a sudden price explosion in futures," one trader said.
"But once the figures have been studied and digested, operators might feel the market has to turn around at some stage."
Traders and analysts last week forecast the German figure five percent higher. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
